A 67-year-old gentleman, recently retired from greenhouse horticulture, entered the diagnostic pathway in early 2022 after an incidental PSA increase. He experiences moderate lower urinary tract symptoms, recording an IPSS score of 18 out of 35, predominantly driven by nocturia and a weak urinary stream, while explicitly denying haematuria or pelvic discomfort. Since losing his spouse several years back, he has maintained a solitary residence, with his adult daughter serving as his main point of contact. Outside urological matters, he manages mild bilateral knee discomfort stemming from prolonged standing during his career, recently completed successful left-eye cataract surgery, and underwent a standard chest radiograph last month. His routine includes a daily twenty-minute walk, weekly alcohol consumption averaging twenty-seven units, and a smoking background of twenty-two pack-years, with cessation dating back to 2012. He reports mild bilateral hearing impairment and requests written documentation for all clinical consultations.
